title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Tb3+ luminescent SMMs need high symmetry to slow the magnetization, and their luminescence-derived gaps are often much larger than the modest magnetic barriers, whereas Tb3+ emission is easier to sensitize and resolve at room temperature than Dy3+ emission.
explanation: As a non-Kramers oblate ion, Tb3+ follows the D4d precedent of [Tb(Pc)2]−. In Zn/Tb Schiff-base and related examples the optical gap greatly exceeds the magnetic barrier (for example about 200 cm−1 versus 4/25 cm−1), which the review attributes to transverse anisotropy. Traditional ligands readily sensitize Tb3+, and resolved bands can be obtained at room temperature, unlike Dy3+ which usually needs low temperature for resolution.
scope: Tb3+ luminescent SMMs, mainly Zn/Tb Schiff-base and related coordination complexes.
conditions: High-symmetry axial coordination; emission analysis of 5D4 → 7F6.
caveats: Reported magnetic barriers in the bifunctional Tb examples are modest, and slow relaxation still requires precise coordination control.
